pr_title: windows_certificate: Add exportable option to pfx certificate
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: dheerajd-msys <dheeraj.dubey@msystechnologies.com>

<!--- Provide a short summary of your changes in the Title above -->
Improvement in the PFX certificate so as to imported certificate can be exported as user wants.
## Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail, what problems does it solve? -->
When we import the PFX certificate, it's unable to export along with its keys so this improvement by adding `exportable` parameter to the underlying function will ensure the certificate to be exportable as well.
- Exported value as integer can be passed to https://github.com/chef/win32-certstore/blob/master/lib/win32/certstore/store_base.rb#L69 so that certificate become exportable.
- Reference doc : https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-pfximportcertstore
## Related Issue

issue_context.title: Add the ability for the windows_certificate resource to be exportable.
issue_context.body:
### Describe the Enhancement:
Add the ability for the `windows_certificate` resource to be exportable.
### Describe the Need:
There is a need from many customers to be able to import a certificate into the Windows Certificate Store and it be marked as `exportable` for certain use cases.
### Current Alternative
Currently, customers are using powershell scripts to accomplish the task of importing the cert, the default when using the `Import-PfxCertificate` is to set the `exportable` flag to `true`, which solves the problem

### Can We Help You Implement This?:
I can provide more specific information as needed. An example import that enables the `exportable` flag looks like this:

`pfx.Import($certPath,$certPass,"Exportable,PersistKeySet")`
comments: This problem is forcing a number of our project to use a powershell script instead of the windows_certificate resource.  We have more of these projects in the pipeline and would appreciate any time that can be put into this.

review_comments: I think this would make more sense to a user if it was true/false instead of an integer.
This needs the introduced field so the documentation will be correctly built
